text: . The Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship will jointly launch tomorrow the second phase of NAVYA – Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls (NAVYA 2.0) in Haridwar, Uttarakhand. The programme will be attended by Union Minister for Women and Child Development Annapurna Devi and Minister of State for Skill Development Jayant Chaudhary.The launch programme of NAVYA 2.0 will also feature the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand and the distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana.NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of both the ministries that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women.

. Myanmar’s military-backed President has said his administration will not fully comply with orders issued by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), which recently ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in 2017. In his first public remarks since the landmark verdict, He said the genocide label had damaged the country’s reputation, adding that Myanmar would reject requirements it considered inappropriate.The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those responsible, prevent further violations and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution. It has also directed the country to facilitate refugee repatriation, restore lost property, locate missing persons and compensate survivors. Myanmar must report on steps taken to implement the orders within two years.The 2017 military crackdown forced more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh, where around 1.2 million refugees remain in camps.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone for second consecutive session today. The Sensex climbed 390 points or half a per cent to close at 84,329. The Nifty rose 65 points or nearly 0.3 per cent to settle at 25,885.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index added 0.3 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index gained over 0.7 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 17 out of 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, Asian Paints shed 2.9 per cent, Bajaj Finance lost over 2.7 per cent, Bajaj Finserv dropped 1.7 per cent. In contrast, HCL Tech surged 6.3 per cent, TCS jumped almost five per cent, and Infosys rose 4.7 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 16 out of 28 sectors edged higher. Among the top gainers, Realty rose three and a half per cent, IT climbed 3.2 per cent, and Metal gained 1.4 per cent. In contrast, Consumer Durables fell over 1.1 per cent, Telecommunication lost nearly one per cent, and Midsmall Private Banks Quality Tilt shed 0.9 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,362 companies advanced, 2,040 declined and 226 remained unchanged.

. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 21 paise to close at 92 rupees and 44 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.79 in intra-day trade.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar today highlighted that the Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity, and economic prosperity. In his opening remarks at the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Council of Ministers meeting in New Delhi, Dr. Jaishankar said it is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and shared challenges. He said IORA’s collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development. He added that in this regard, India’s approach to IORA and India’s Chairship of the Association is guided by Vision MAHASAGAR, that is, mutual and holistic advancement for security and growth across regions.The External Affairs Minister said that at a time of significant global challenges, IORA must enhance its collective voice and reinforce its role as an inclusive regional platform. He stressed that achieving this requires greater coordination among member states, meaningful collaboration with dialogue partners, and a strong focus on practical cooperation.Dr. Jaishankar said India’s Chairship theme is ‘Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region.’ He stated that these principles reflect New Delhi’s conviction that IORA must remain responsive and adaptive to the changing regional and global environment while delivering tangible benefits to its member states. He added that during its Chairship, India is trying to strengthen cooperation across IORA’s priority areas and cross-cutting issues, deepen engagement with dialogue partners, promote practical regional initiatives and advance financial and institutional strengthening of the Association. He said that a stronger institutional foundation is essential for IORA to fulfil its larger role in the region.This is the first Council of Ministers Meeting under the chairship of India. Dr. Jaishankar expressed appreciation to Sri Lanka for its leadership as the previous chair of IORA and welcomed Mauritius as the Vice Chair and Future Chair of the Association. He said India looks forward to working closely with both countries and all stakeholders in advancing shared objectives.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold rose 1.3 per cent to 1,22,641 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver increased 3.1 per cent to 1,47, 347 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. Major Asian stock market indices ended on a positive note today. Taiwan’s Taiex surged two and a half per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 1.2 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.9 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times added nearly 0.7 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi increased 0.3 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite eked out a marginal gain.Meanwhile, the Bank of Korea (BOK) raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage points to 3.25 per cent. The decision was taken in a 5-2 vote at the monetary policy meeting today. According to BOK, the Gross Domestic Product is projected to reach 3.9 per cent this year, while headline CPI inflation is expected to stand at 2.7 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose 1.9 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 gained over one and a half per cent, when reports last came in.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar met his Sri Lankan counterpart Vijitha Herath in New Delhi. They discussed bilateral ties and the situation in the region. Dr. Jaishankar said that he looks forward to their further discussions at the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA). The Minister also met his Maldivian counterpart, Iruthisham Adam. They both exchanged notes on the progress of India-Maldives ties and touched upon multilateral, security and development cooperation.Earlier, Dr. Jaishankar held a meeting with the Foreign Minister of Seychelles, Barry Faure, in New Delhi. They reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthening people-centric partnerships focusing on health, connectivity, skilling, energy, cyber and AI. Both Ministers also discussed cooperation in the Indian Ocean Rim IORA) and regional issues.The External Affairs Minister also met his Mauritius counterpart Dhananjay Ramful and reviewed key areas of the bilateral relationship, including progress under the Special Economic Package. Both Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the India-Mauritius Enhanced Strategic Partnership and supporting Mauritius’ development priorities under India’s Vision MAHASAGAR and Neighbourhood First Policy.

. In the latest ICC Men’s Test Player Rankings, India’s batting performance in the drawn first Test against New Zealand has led to a major reshuffle. Rishabh Pant remains India’s highest-ranked batter, moving up one place to sixth following his 128-run knock. Test captain Shubman Gill climbed three places to seventh, while Yashasvi Jaiswal jumped five places to ninth. KL Rahul advanced four places to 25th after scoring 136, while Devdutt Padikkal rose 15 places to 39th following his 80-run contribution. India’s pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah also gained three places to reach joint-second in the bowling rankings.Among New Zealand batters, Henry Nicholls climbed 10 places to 30th, while Glenn Phillips rose 13 places to a career-best 17th.In other movements, Bangladesh’s Towhid Hridoy advanced 28 places to 33rd and Litton Das moved up to 24th. South Africa’s Ryan Rickelton reached a career-best joint-15th, while Kagiso Rabada climbed to sixth among bowlers after his eight-wicket match haul against Bangladesh. The latest rankings update reflects performances in the first Tests between India and New Zealand, South Africa and Bangladesh, and the second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, in Goa is highlighting the growing contribution of women to cinema. 52 women filmmakers are participating in this year’s festival.Indian women filmmakers are leading from the front, bringing diverse narratives and fresh perspectives.Leena Yadav’s Ladakhi film Becoming explores themes of spirituality and destiny. While, Muskan Asthana’s Sev Micchar, Anupama Sharadhi’s Pili Channe and Antara G G Choudhury’s Surjyamukhi further add to the diversity of Indian storytelling.The festival is also showcasing compelling voices from across the world. Kyrgyz filmmaker Narghiza Dotieva’s Skylark explores the impact of border disputes on a teenager’s life. Romanian-Roma filmmaker Alina Șerban’s film I Matter was the mid-fest film. In a media interaction Sherban, who has roots in India, became emotional.From challenging stereotypes and examining social realities to exploring identity, culture and women’s experiences, these filmmakers are bringing fresh perspectives to the screen.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. India and Sri Lanka have concluded their joint military exercise MITRA SHAKTI, strengthening defence cooperation and operational coordination between the two armed forces. The 12th edition of the bilateral exercise was held at the Army Training School in Maduru Oya, with more than 350 personnel from both countries participating.The final demonstration showcased joint operational capabilities and training in coordinated military operations. Senior military officers from Sri Lanka and representatives of the Indian High Commission witnessed the demonstration. The exercise focused on enhancing interoperability, mutual understanding and the ability of the two forces to operate together.MITRA SHAKTI is among the key bilateral military engagements between India and Sri Lanka. The exercise has also evolved into a broader, two-service engagement, reflecting the growing scope of defence cooperation between the neighbouring countries. The latest edition reinforces India’s and Sri Lanka’s commitment to strengthening military ties and regional security cooperation.

. Union Minister of Finance  Nirmala Sitharaman  has   concluded the  extensive pre-budget consultation meetings for the preparation of the Union Budget 2027-28. Ms Sitharaman today chaired the 13th and final Pre-Budget Consultation with youth for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The first consultation meeting was held on 16th of this month. Ministry of Finance has said that more than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the consultations.These include industry associations, domain experts,  youth representatives and practitioners from Agriculture and Rural Development; Manufacturing, MSMEs and Startups; Capital Markets and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance, Information Technology, Infrastructure, Energy and Sustainability and Employment and Labour.The consultation meeting with youth representatives was a novel initiative this year. The Ministry said that the the consultations generated a wide range of forward-looking recommendations aimed at strengthening India’s human capital, innovation ecosystem, manufacturing competitiveness, agricultural productivity, housing security, and educational outcomes. Stakeholders emphasized the need for reforms that can further accelerate economic growth while ensuring broad-based and inclusive development.Collectively, the recommendations focused on promoting innovation-led growth, expanding employment opportunities, strengthening social and economic infrastructure, and building a more resilient and future-ready economy.The pre-budget consultations form an important part of the Government’s participatory and consultative approach to budget-making, enabling diverse stakeholders to contribute to shaping India’s development priorities and growth agenda.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India in Goa enters its eighth day today, with a star-studded panel discussion, filmmaker interactions and an exciting line-up of films adding to the celebrations. With just two days remaining, the festival continues to bring together celebrated filmmakers, emerging talent and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. Today’s highlights include a special discussion featuring Farhan Akhtar, Ashutosh Gowariker and Madhur Bhandarkar, along with the screening of the much-awaited first episode of Panchayat Season Five.From celebrating iconic films to exploring new cinematic possibilities, Day Eight of IFFI promises another exciting journey through the world of cinema.The spotlight will be on The Legendary 25s, a panel discussion featuring filmmaker and actor Farhan Akhtar, filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker and director Madhur Bhandarkar. The session will revisit the cinematic journey and legacy of three landmark films released in 2001: Dil Chahta Hai, Lagaan and Chandni Bar. Later in the afternoon, filmmaker Karthik Subbaraj will take part in an interactive session titled ‘What if the Villain is Right?’, exploring unconventional perspectives in filmmaking.Adding to the excitement for audiences, the first episode of Panchayat Season Five, directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, will have a special screening at INOX Panjim. The festival will also feature a diverse selection of Indian and international films across its screening venues. Open-air screenings will continue at Miramar Beach, Vagator Beach and Ravindra Bhavan in Margao, bringing the cinematic experience closer to the public.As IFFI moves towards its grand finale tomorrow, Goa continues to celebrate the universal language of cinema under this year’s theme, “Stories Without Borders.”

. The semi-final matches of the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy will be played today in Bhopal. Hosts and defending champions India will face Malaysia at 7 PM. South Korea will take on Thailand at 2 PM, while Japan will play against China at 4:30 PM.India topped the league stage with 15 points after winning all five matches. The team has scored 23 goals and conceded only four. Deepika is India’s leading scorer with eight goals. She has also scored hat-tricks against Thailand and China. Captain Salima Tete and Navneet Kaur have also played important roles in the team’s performance.India defeated Malaysia 4-1 in their league match on November 19. However, Malaysia also secured a place in the semi-finals after defeating Thailand 4-0 in its last league match. The Indian women’s team has won the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in 2016, 2023, and 2024. India now has a chance to win its fourth title in Bhopal and become the most successful team in the tournament.

. The Supreme Court today granted four weeks of interim bail to Aam Aadmi Party leader Deepak Singla in connection with a money laundering case stemming from an alleged 155-crore-rupee bank fraud.A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed the order after noting that Singla had already spent over six months in custody and that a co-accused in the matter had already been granted bail.The Court also asked the Punjab and Haryana High Court to decide Singla’s pending plea challenging his arrest and seeking bail within a four-week window.

. In Cricket, Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets to reach the final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha last night. Chasing a target of 318 runs, Sri Lanka A scored 318 runs with the loss of 2 wickets in 41.3 overs against India A in the first semi-final. Opting to bat first, India A scored 317 runs, losing 8 wickets in the stipulated 50 overs. For India A, Abhishek Sharma scored the highest score, 78 runs off 63 balls. Since Jayawardena was declared player of the match. Sri Lanka: A opener, Sineth, scored 105 off 70 balls.Sri Lanka A will play the final on Sunday. The opponent will be decided today, when Pakistan A faces Bangladesh A in the 2nd Semi-Final at 3:30 PM IST in Doha.

. In three-key matches of the 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament played last evening at Jalandhar, Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala) secured a commanding 4-1 victory over BSF Jalandhar, while the match between Bharat Petroleum and the Army (Delhi) ended in a 0-0 draw. Punjab Police team defeated Indian Navy (Mumbai) by 4-1.So far in the tournament, teams of Indian Oil, Punjab Police, Punjab National Bank (Delhi), Indian Air Force, Bharat Petroleum, Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala), Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi), and CAG (Delhi) have secured their spots in the quarter-finals.In today’s 4 quarter-final matches, Indian Oil (Mumbai) will play with Punjab National Bank (Delhi) at 12:00 PM. Indian Air Force will take on CAG (Delhi) at 2:00 PM. Bharat Petroleum (Mumbai) will face Rail Coach Factory (Kapurthala) at 3:30 PM and Punjab Police will dribble with Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi) at 5:30 PM.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand finished the opening day of the second Test against India at 246 for five at stumps in Christchurch. Tom Blundell on 53 runs and Glenn Phillips on 36 runs were at the crease when stumps were drawn today. For India, Akash Deep claimed two wickets, while Gurnoor Brar, Washington Sundar and Anshul Kamboj picked up one wicket each. Earlier, Indian captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl. India made just one change to their playing 11, handing Gurnoor Brar his Test debut in place of Prasidh Krishna. while New Zealand remained unchanged. The first Test between the two sides had ended in a draw.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced new measures to simplify client onboarding and streamline risk management at KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs). In a circular issued today, the market regulator announced that common client details, such as income range, occupation, CKYC ID, and DIGIPIN, will now be centralised at the KRA level to prevent duplication across intermediaries.Under the revised norms, separate mobile verification will be optional if the number is already Aadhaar-seeded and verified in the KRA database. Investors will also no longer need separate proof for a name change if it is already updated in their PAN and Aadhaar records. Additionally, overseas address proof will be optional for resident OCI cardholders and foreign nationals who provide verified Indian address proof.To enhance data privacy, intermediaries must now report account closures to KRAs within five working days. These new provisions will take effect from 24th December 2026.

. India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission.The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by the city, state, and central authorities to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games.Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye are the other countries that are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid. The survey is expected to be done in the third week of December and will have a bearing on the evaluation of India’s bid in March next year, following which the phase of Strategic Dialogue will start. During this phase, the interested countries will be expected to provide an initial response to the Future Host Questionnaire and core financial guarantees.

. Border Security Force (BSF) troops neutralised a Pakistani intruder along the International Border with Pakistan in Punjab’s Pathankot in the wee hours today. According to officials, the troops saw a movement near its Pahadipur Border out Post (BOP) at 2.00 AM as the intruder entered inside Indian territory. Despite issuing warnings to stop he kept walking in forcing the BSF to fire. Pathankot police are investigating the incident.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast dense fog conditions over Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and northeastern parts of the country today. IMD has also predicted cold wave conditions over East Rajasthan till tomorrow. The Met Department said that Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to experience heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds today. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also expected over Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep till tomorrow.

. In Chess, reigning world champion D Gukesh played out a quick 20-move draw with Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva yesterday.Playing with white, Gukesh opted for the London System but failed to gain an advantage as Sindarov comfortably equalised. The Indian agreed to a draw by threefold repetition, with all 30 remaining pieces still on the board.Both players are now level at one point each after two games of the 14-game championship match.The third game will be played tomorrow, with Sindarov having the white pieces.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today said that a healthy India is the foundation of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Vice President said this after inaugurating the New Super Speciality Block of Holy Family Hospital in New Delhi. He called for a collective fight against cancer and social evils like the drug mafia. Mr Radhakrishnan highlighted the need for collaborative efforts in cancer care and research. He emphasised that medical advancements must benefit all sections of society and called upon healthcare institutions to combine medical excellence with affordability, compassion and a human touch.Highlighting the transformation in India’s health infrastructure over the past decade, Mr Radhakrishnan said that the number of medical colleges across the country have increased from 387 to 846. He noted that schemes like Ayushman Bharat have reduced the financial burden on poor families, with around two lakh crore rupees disbursed for healthcare coverage, and emphasised expanding health insurance access further.

. India will host the 25th Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Council of Ministers Meeting in New Delhi today. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Seychelles Barry Faure, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mauritius Dhananjay Ramful, and Sri Lankan Foreign Affairs Minister Vijitha Herath will participate in the IORA Council of Ministers Meeting, among others. The theme for India’s IORA chairship 2025-2027 is “Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region.”This high-level gathering of Ministers and Senior Officials from across the 23 Member States and 12 Dialogue Partners comes at a critical juncture for the Indo-Pacific region. It is slated to deliberate on future policy direction for IORA with an emphasis on reviewing regional cooperation frameworks and identifying new areas of collaboration.The New Delhi Meeting will underscore the vital importance of the Indian Ocean Region as a region of peace, stability, predictability and sustainable development. It will reaffirm India’s commitment to the vision of MAHASAGAR, driving collective action for an open, inclusive, and rules-based maritime order. IORA is an intergovernmental organization established on 7th March, 1997, to promote regional cooperation and sustainable development around the Indian Ocean.

. The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has become the world’s third-largest listed stock exchange by market capitalisation, overtaking Germany’s Deutsche Boerse and the London Stock Exchange Group.According to the latest market data, NSE’s market capitalisation stands at around 64.1 billion US dollars. It is ahead of Deutsche Boerse at 63.4 billion dollars and London Stock Exchange Group at 62.4 billion dollars.The global ranking is led by CME Group with a market capitalisation of 111.6 billion dollars, followed by Intercontinental Exchange at 99.4 billion dollars.NSE shares were trading at 2,369 rupees and 65 paise, up 2.24 per cent today. The stock has gained around 32 per cent since its listing on September 24.The milestone further strengthens NSE’s position among the world’s leading stock exchange operators.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading 0.8 per cent up at 95 US dollars and 38 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.2 per cent higher at 84 US dollars and 65 cent per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The NCP (SP) has issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30 during the upcoming special session of Parliament.The three-line whip, issued by the party’s chief whip Amol Kolhe, said, “As very important business will be taken up in the Lok Sabha from November 30 to December 4, all Lok Sabha members of the NCP (SP) are requested to remain present in the House without fail and support the party’s stand.”The whip comes amid the buzz that the party may support the government on the delimitation bill.NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule has maintained that her party, which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, may consider the proposal if the number of seats in all states is increased by a uniform 50 per cent.

. Reigning world champion D. Gukesh held challenger Javokhir Sindarov to a draw with the black pieces in Game 3 of the 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship in Geneva yesterday. The players are now tied at 1.5 points apiece heading into today’s rest day.Gukesh looked well prepared for the opening and handled Sindarov’s attempts to gain an advantage with confidence. Even when computer evaluations suggested that white had the upper hand, the Indian appeared to know exactly where to find the right moves and how to keep his position intact. The draw also leaves him with the white pieces in the next game.With 11 games still remaining in the 14-game match, it appears Gukesh has a few surprises up his sleeve in terms of preparation, while Sindarov has some questions to answer about his own match preparation. As per the rules, the first player to reach 7.5 points will win the title. In case of a 7-7 tie after 14 games, shorter-format games will be played to determine the winner.

. BJP leader and Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Brajesh Pathak has termed the Samajwadi Party’s manifesto released for the upcoming Assembly polls as a hollow document and a bundle of lies. Briefing reporters in New Delhi, Mr. Pathak alleged that whenever the Samajwadi Party had been in power in the state, criminals, goons and mafias had flourished under its rule. He also raised questions about SP’s concern for farmers, the poor and the youth. Mr. Pathak said that the Party should not release a manifesto but an apology letter to the people of the state.

. The Indian women’s hockey team continued its impressive winning run at the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy, securing a convincing 4-0 victory over Japan in Bhopal ahead of the semi-finals.Deepika starred with two goals, while Lalremsiami and Neha added one goal each to seal India’s emphatic win. Navneet Kaur was named Player of the Match and dedicated the award to the entire team. India’s impressive campaign has also propelled the team to fourth place in the world rankings, providing an additional boost ahead of the knockout stage.In the other matches, Malaysia defeated Thailand 4-0, while China secured a narrow 1-0 win over Korea.India will now face Malaysia in the semi-final on tomorrow, as the hosts aim to continue their winning run and move closer to the title. The tournament will conclude on November 28, with the bronze-medal match at 4:30 PM, followed by the final at 7 PM.

. President Droupadi Murmu has called for strengthening India’s traditional systems of medicine through scientific research, documentation and institutional collaboration. She was addressing the valedictory ceremony of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College at Thrissur in Keralam today.The President highlighted Keralam’s rich Ayurvedic heritage and appreciated the contribution of the Ashtavaidya families in preserving and promoting classical Ayurvedic knowledge. She emphasised the need to systematically document ancient texts, manuscripts, treatment methods and traditional practices.Smt. Murmu said Ayurvedic colleges should undertake joint research projects with government institutions and international agencies to strengthen evidence-based healthcare. She also stressed the need to develop authentic and scientifically evaluated Panchakarma practices, adding that Keralam has the potential to emerge as an international centre for the same.The President said every Ayurvedic institution should focus on providing effective healthcare to the community while imparting contemporary education to students. She expressed confidence that such efforts would contribute to the vision of a healthy and developed India by 2047. Addressing students, she urged them to uphold the tradition of combining professional excellence with service to the underprivileged.During the ceremony, the President unveiled the logo of ‘Prana’, a Golden Jubilee initiative aimed at promoting Ayurvedic healthcare for mothers and children through an integration of traditional knowledge and modern advancements. The Governor of Keralam, Union Minister of State Suresh Gopi and other dignitaries attended the event.

. India defeated Japan 4-NIL in the last league-stage matches of the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. Indian women’s team has topped the group stage of the tournament. Meanwhile, the Indian women’s Hockey team has climbed to 4th place in the FIH rankings, its highest-ever position since the world body introduced the system in October 2003.

. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has said that the government will bring significant legislative business in the Lok Sabha during its four-day sittings, which is to begin from Monday. Talking to the media in New Delhi ahead of the special sittings of both the Houses of Parliament, Mr. Rijiju said that these legislations will be further introduced in the sittings of the Rajya Sabha beginning on the 2nd of December.Mr Rijiju said that he held discussions with the leaders of major political parties and has also appealed to all the political parties in this regard. Mr. Rijiju also rejected the allegations of some MPs that the government does not follow established rules, saying that the government can convene a special sitting or session of Parliament for important legislative business, and it has also been the practice earlier.Mr. Rijiju also requested the leaders of all political parties and every Member of Parliament to engage wholeheartedly in the discussion on the bills to be introduced. He said it is the responsibility of all Members of Parliament to ensure that the proceedings of both the Houses run smoothly.

. Union Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Jitan Ram Manjhi, said that the government’s focus has shifted from helping small businesses survive to making them globally competitive. He said that the government aim is to enable MSMEs to expand their presence worldwide.Addressing the 12th FICCI Confederation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (FICCI-CMSME) Annual Summit 2026 in New Delhi, the Minister highlighted the MSME sector’s contribution of around 31 per cent to India’s GDP, 35 per cent to manufacturing output and nearly 50 per cent to total exports. He emphasized on providing equal opportunities to every MSME unit, irrespective of geographical or social background, to participate in India’s economic transformation

. The 57th International Film Festival of India is marking its seventh day in Goa with tributes to cinematic legends, masterclasses and special film screenings. The festival today honoured veteran actor Nana Patekar through a special screening of his acclaimed film Diksha, as part of the Homage section.Day Seven of the 57th International Film Festival of India opens on an exciting note as Rishab Shetty’s much-awaited Kannada film Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1 is being screened this morning in the International Competition section.Directed by and starring Rishab Shetty, the 169-minute film follows Berme, a young forest dweller, who enters the neighbouring kingdom of Bangra and witnesses the oppression of forest communities by its rulers. When Prince Kulashekara launches an attack on the tribes, Berme joins their struggle for justice and dharma.Blending spectacular visuals, indigenous traditions, and action, the film brings a distinctive cultural narrative from India’s regional cinema to an international platform.With Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1 competing alongside films from across the world, IFFI once again highlights how deeply rooted local stories can find a universal audience through the language of cinema.Acclaimed casting director and filmmaker Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged’ at Kala Academy, Panaji, on the seventh day today as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). During the 90-minute session, Chhabra spoke about how actors are chosen for films, the importance of auditions and the process of finding the right person for each role. Sharing his experiences from films such as Rockstar, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Dangal, Jawan and Dhurandhar, he spoke about finding new talent from different parts of the country and understanding what a director wants from a character.Blending creativity, technology and innovation, the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) is drawing attention at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) with a showcase of emerging opportunities in the creative technology sector. Established by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, IICT is a national-level institute dedicated to Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR).The stall offers visitors a glimpse into the growing possibilities in these fields, highlighting career opportunities, academic programmes and skill development initiatives. It also showcases the institute’s efforts in startup incubation, policy development and research aimed at strengthening India’s creative technology ecosystem.Adding an interactive touch to the showcase, the stall features the ‘Doodle Dash: The Movie Poster Challenge’, a creative competition inviting participants to bring movie posters to life through their artistic skills. The challenge offers prizes worth over one lakh rupees, along with scholarships of up to 30 per cent on IICT’s two-year programmes.Through its academic and innovation-driven initiatives, IICT aims to nurture skilled talent, encourage creative entrepreneurship and support the growth of India’s AVGC-XR industry.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced new measures to simplify client onboarding and streamline risk management at KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs). In a circular issued yesterday, the market regulator announced that common client details, such as income range, occupation, CKYC ID, and DIGIPIN, will now be centralised at the KRA level to prevent duplication across intermediaries.Under the revised norms, separate mobile verification will be optional if the number is already Aadhaar-seeded and verified in the KRA database. Investors will also no longer need separate proof for a name change if it is already updated in their PAN and Aadhaar records. Additionally, overseas address proof will be optional for resident OCI cardholders and foreign nationals who provide verified Indian address proof.To enhance data privacy, intermediaries must now report account closures to KRAs within five working days. These new provisions will take effect from 24th December 2026.

. Iran has denied involvement in the attacks on Kuwait that resulted in the death of two Italian Nationals. Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence had yesterday reported that 2 Italians were killed in Iranian drone attacks that targeted a vital site in Kuwait. However, Iran’s embassy in Rome has rejected the allegation that Iran was behind the purported drone attack on a military facility in Kuwait. Iran’s Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi also called the incident suspicious and said they are ready to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause of the incident.In Saudi Arabia, the Jazan oil refinery temporarily halted operations after an aerial projectile struck the facility, causing a fire. The Saudi Press Agency has reported that a Nepalese worker was killed and several others were injured in this attack. Jazan hosts a massive refinery and petrochemical complex on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia.

. Belgian filmmaker Isabelle Tollenaere today expressed happiness over the reception of her film ‘Paris Paris’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa. Addressing a press conference, Ms Tollenaere said that it was her first visit to India and that she felt honoured to present her film to Indian audiences. She said the film received an encouraging response during its screening, which was attended by a full house, followed by an engaging question-and-answer session.Sharing insights into the filmmaking process, Ms Tollenaere said her background in documentary filmmaking influenced her approach to casting, with actors chosen for their similarities to the real-life backgrounds of the characters they portray. She also revealed that her grandparents, who were immigrants, served as an inspiration for the film.‘Paris Paris’, featured in the International Cinema category at IFFI, tells the story of three men from different backgrounds who attempt to build a home together in a squatted apartment in Paris. Through their conversations about the past and the future, the film explores themes of displacement, identity and belonging.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today said that the trade deal between India and the United States is now being finalized and close to culmination. Speaking at the India Debt Capital Market Summit virtually in New Delhi, Mr. Goyal said that the bilateral deal was held back due to some processes but is now at its final stage. The Minister expressed hope that the India-EU FTA will be executed and signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year.Mr. Goyal said that over the past five years, India has finalized nine Free Trade Agreements covering 38 developed countries, taking its preferential market access to economies with a combined GDP of 70 trillion dollars. He noted that another eight or nine agreements under negotiation could expand this to 85 trillion dollars. In the domestic economy, the Minister said that India has maintained its growth momentum despite global uncertainties, including conflicts, oil price shocks and tariff-related disruptions.Mr. Goyal said that exports have reached approximately  570 billion dollars in the first seven months of the financial year, putting India on track to achieve its 1 trillion dollars annual export target. He noted that October exports touched a record nearly 90 billion dollars.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. India is providing financial assistance of around eight crore 90 lakh Nepali rupees for the construction of a new school building, teachers’ quarters and a hostel at Shree Janabal Secondary School in Nepal’s Mustang district. The foundation stone for the project was jointly laid yesterday (26th November) by Dr. Rakesh Pandey, Charge d’Affaires at the Embassy of India in Kathmandu, and Mohan Singh Lalchan, Chairman of Gharapjhong Rural Municipality.The project, located in Gharapjhong-2 of Gandaki Province, will be implemented through the local rural municipality under the Government of India’s High Impact Community Development Project program. It will be the 18th project undertaken by India in the Mustang district under this initiative.The assistance reflects the close development partnership between India and Nepal. Through these projects, India supports Nepal’s development by strengthening infrastructure in key sectors, including education.

. Three buses were set on fire by unidentified individuals in Bangladesh’s capital, Dhaka, last night, raising fresh security concerns. The incidents were reported in the Mirpur and Badda areas.One of the buses, operated by Bihanga Paribahan, was torched on Kalshi-Purabi Road in Pallabi while returning to its stand after dropping off passengers. The fire damaged its seats and upper section. Local residents managed to bring the blaze under control before firefighters arrived. Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jalal Uddin said no one was injured in the incident and that police were working to identify those responsible.Earlier, at around 6:30 pm, a parked Madhumati Paribahan bus was set ablaze near Bihari Millat Camp in Section 11 of Pallabi. In a separate incident, an Alif Paribahan bus was torched near Canadian University in Badda at around 9:50 pm. Fire Service personnel later brought the blaze under control.No casualties were reported in any of the three incidents.

. Acclaimed casting director and filmmaker Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged’ at Kala Academy, Panaji, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).During the 90-minute session, Chhabra spoke about how actors are chosen for films, the importance of auditions and the process of finding the right person for each role. Sharing his experiences from films such as Rockstar, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Dangal, Jawan and Dhurandhar, he spoke about finding new talent from different parts of the country and understanding what a director wants from a character.Addressing aspiring actors, Chhabra said, “Rejection is part of life. I don’t reject an actor, I only reject a character. My job is to fit with the director’s vision.” He encouraged young actors to keep working hard, learn from every opportunity and not give up after rejection. “Auditions can change your life,” he said, adding that actors should be open to guidance and direction.Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker praised Chhabra, calling people like him an asset to the film industry. Recalling the making of Lagaan, Gowariker said finding the right actors was a real struggle, as professional casting directors were not part of the process in the way they are today. He spoke about how casting directors help filmmakers find the right actors for their stories.Chhabra, who also directed Dil Bechara, recalled how Gangs of Wasseypur changed his life.The masterclass was part of IFFI’s knowledge-sharing sessions under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’.

. Today is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The day is observed on November 25 every year to raise awareness about violence against women and girls and call for an end to abuse and discrimination. This year, the United Nations marks the day under the theme, UNITE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity.The theme highlights the need for stronger justice systems, safe reporting mechanisms, better support services for survivors and accountability for perpetrators. It also recognizes that violence against women takes place in homes, workplaces, public spaces and online.According to the UN, one in three women worldwide experiences physical or sexual violence during her lifetime. However, many survivors still struggle to access justice, protection and support due to fear, social stigma, discrimination and weak institutional responses.

. Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “Make in India” vision during his interaction with young Indian AI innovator Raul John Aju at the AI Journey conference in Moscow. Connecting Aju’s AI projects to PM Modi’s initiative, Putin remarked that such work helps realise the “Make in India” call by enabling young people to find and implement their own local solutions. This interaction highlights how young innovators from India are making a mark on the world stage.

. India and UAE have agreed to accelerate co-development and co-production of next-generation defence equipment. The 14th meeting of the India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee (JDCC) took place in Abu Dhabi yesterday. The meeting was co-chaired by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh from the Indian side and Under Secretary, Ministry of Defence, UAE, Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi.According to the Ministry of Defence, the meeting provided strategic direction to the initiatives laid out in the India-UAE Strategic Defence Partnership Framework signed in May 2026 during the visit of the Prime Minister to the UAE. Both sides agreed to enhance bilateral defence ties under a wide range of areas, specifically defence industry, defence innovation & advanced technology, artificial intelligence, cyber, military training and maritime safety.​​They agreed to accelerate co-development and co-production partnerships in next-generation defence equipment. The co-chairs decided to review the progress made in defence cooperation at regular intervals in the interim before the next JDCC. The Indian delegation comprised representatives from the Department of Defence, Indian Defence Forces, National Security Council Secretariat and Ministry of External Affairs.

Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.
